headline: C2, D1, D2, D3 ALL REPRODUCE AS PASSES in both a clean arm and a hostiles-present arm — the save defect never made them failures, and the round-1 verdict never filed them as such. ARBITRATION S38 then landed mid-round and rules the forged-save question out of scope; that axis is WITHDRAWN, not scored, and its gate re-verified independently (6/6, control exit 1). What survives is S38 clause (d): the load audit is computed and never published, and the S38 gate cannot see it because S38-4 only ever forges the claim fields.
findings: PROCEDURAL FAILURE OF MINE, RECORDED: I missed ARBITRATION S38 on my first pass. I grepped ARBITRATION.md for 'S35' and read that row; S38 is the row IMMEDIATELY BELOW IT and it amends S35 in place, ruling that S35's clause binds the map's DERIVATION and the game's authoring surface, not the authenticity of a save file, and that 'a critic may not fail a build for a forged footprint'. I found it only when `node tools/ownership.mjs --staged` named an arbiter's staged screenshot. RULES 18 says read the file; a grep is not reading the file. Nothing measured is affected, but an entire axis was re-cut, and the first draft of this verdict would have failed the build for a property a landed ruling puts out of scope.
PREMISE VERIFIED (P1): at f291b01 a save/load with 3 hostiles present keeps a live SoulsAI (ctor SoulsAI -> SoulsAI, 3 -> 3 live) and 60 fixed steps run with 0 faults. The W1-SAVE-AI fix holds.

CONTROL VERIFIED (P3, rule 6): replacing a live ctl.ai with a plain object makes my fault detector fire with the exact pre-fix message 'this.ai.step is not a function'. Every '0 faults' figure below is from a detector that has been watched going red.

THE BRIEF'S PREMISE IS OVERSTATED, and the source it comes from says so. W1-SAVE-AI.json:91 says 'The critic caught the misattribution, but C2/D1/D2/D3 are worth re-taking'. W1-MAP-r1.md's own table lists C2/D1/D2/D3 as PASSES, and its §9 records that they first appeared as failures and that C0/D0 preconditions stopped them being filed. No false finding was ever published.

RE-TAKE RESULT: C2, D1, D2, D3 all PASS, identically, in a clean arm and in an arm with 3 live hostile AIs on the floor (R-agree). 0 step faults in each arm, frames advanced in each arm, 2106 vs 2115 cells drawn. The findings are properties of the map, not of the save.

A9 — THE FORGED SAVE IS WORSE THAN ROUND 1 RECORDED. Round 1 handed a forged object to loadState(). A9 writes a real save container with the game's OWN save/exchange.js exportSave() (which computes the sha-256 the reader verifies) and reads it back through importSave(): 124,898 sealed bytes ACCEPTED, place_count 42/42, revealed 42,846/42,846, 42 squares drawn. The player-facing route is open.

A12a/A12b — the seal is an INTEGRITY check, not an AUTHENTICITY check. Editing sealed bytes is refused ('the seal does not match'). Resealing the forgery with the game's own writer is ACCEPTED. An unkeyed sha-256 stops corruption, not a forger.

A10 — the forgery is NOT an artefact of the broken load. After importing it, 2 hostiles spawned and 180 fixed steps ran with 0 faults and the map stayed at 42/42 places, 42,846/42,846 cells. A round-1 forged-save pass could have been a load that died; this one is not.

A11 — THE HOLE IS OPEN AND THE REPORT IS CLOSED. On the fully forged state every published compliance number reads clean: places_drawn 42 == places_discovered 42, markers 0, routes 0, numerals 0, travel 0, quest_bearing 0, dropped_on_load 0. Nothing the build publishes distinguishes a forged map from an honest one.

A5 — the signal already exists and is thrown away. Discovery.restore() computes dropped, phantom_cells, missing_cells, claimed_places, derived_places, stood_cells, legacy. save/state.js:676 keeps only .dropped; mapState() publishes only dropped_on_load. Published footprint-audit fields: NONE. This is round 1's remedy 1, not done.
Q1/Q2 — sim.discovery is still writable:true configurable:true and questEngine.sim === sim. Installing a substitute model through the object the quest machine itself holds draws 3 squares.

Q3 — THE BACK DOOR THE BRIEF NAMES IS OPEN. window.__ENGINE.sim.discovery = <forged> draws 2 squares, and getCapabilityReport() does not mention __ENGINE at all, so capability prohibitions do not cover it.
Q4 PASSES: no method ON the model accepts a place. 13 attempts, 0 succeeded, requested place absent, place list unchanged.

STATIC HALF OF C: nothing under game/src/sim/quest/ reaches a map module. grep for map|discovery|__ENGINE|reveal|marker|Discovery over all 8 files returns only quest-internal reveal() (a know: flag), Array.prototype.map, and one S35 comment. The reachable route is the writable slot, not a call.

U1/U2/U3 — undiscovered is genuinely UNRENDERED. Empty map: 1 distinct colour over 345,071 px, drawn_cells 0, and per-channel range [0,0,0] — a drawn-then-masked province cannot produce that. screens/map.js:103 is `if (!m.seen(cx,rz)) continue;`, so the geometry is never in the scene.

E3/E4/E5/E6 — hover names hold. Being told about a place through questEngine.learnFrom('place'), setWorldKnowledge and learnTopic changes nothing. One square per place, unique. The name is that place's own pois.json name. markers/routes/numerals/travel/quest_bearing all 0 and the map is not reachable from the journal.

G2 — CONSUMPTION FAILS. World hash (discovery blob excluded) is c23bbb77:52365 in both arms; ablating the model entirely changes nothing in the running world. The only consumer is the map's own draw call.

THREE OF MY OWN CHECKS WERE WRONG AND WERE REPAIRED BEFORE FILING. (1) E3 read placeCount 0 -> 1 after the 'tell' attempts, which reads exactly like a build defect; it was my baseline, taken before the first step, and the default start position is inside LILMOTH's own pad. (2) E5 asserted the hover name must be 'Thorn'; the naming element names places[placeIdx], which is the first place found, i.e. Lilmoth. (3) Q4 saw the place list move because tryPlaceMapMarker ends by calling d.observe(4600,5200) to show surplus arguments are ignored, and observe() records the cell the body is in. (4) A12 originally PASSED by matching the substring 'signature' in the save manifest, which is regionSignature/focusSignature — an inert check that passed for the wrong reason. All four repaired and documented in the tool.

AND A CORRECTION TO THAT LAST NUMBER, WHICH IS ALSO A CORRECTION TO W1-MAP-r1. U1/U2's '1 colour, channel range [0,0,0]' is read off UISurface.ctx.getImageData — the interface's OWN 2D canvas — and so is r1's C1/C3. It is true of the UI layer and FALSE of the picture: the panel is drawn at CALM_ALPHA over the running 3D world and the Rootlands are visible through the black box in docs/shots/2026-08-08-critic-map-r2-fresh.png. On the composited frame the same box holds 44 distinct colours. S35 still holds, but it is carried by screens/map.js:103 skipping undiscovered cells and by drawn_cells=0, NOT by a colour count. tools/harness/critic-map-r2-composite.mjs separates the causes 5/5: two EMPTY maps photographed from different standing places differ (44 -> 92 colours, drawn_cells 0 -> 0, so the variation is the scene behind the panel), and the same standing place with a walked body differs the other way (44 -> 1855, drawn_cells 0 -> 2911).

map-probe.mjs is 32/32 AT THE SAME COMMIT and its L3 — 'a FORGED save naming a place the raster does not corroborate is refused' — is GREEN, because map-probe.mjs:440 still forges world.discovery.places, the field Discovery.RESTORE_READS was narrowed to EXCLUDE. Round 1's remedy 2, not done. A green 32/32 and 42 phantom squares on the same tree in the same hour.

A13 — THE ONE S38 CLAUSE THAT SURVIVES MY ATTACK, and its own gate cannot see it. S38(d) requires 'a discrepancy between the blob's claims and the derivation is ITEMISED, not swallowed'. S38-4 verifies it by forging the CLAIM FIELDS (all-ones raster, all 42 names) and reading dropped=41, phantom_cells=41566. But the forgery a forger would write supplies NO claims: with cells:"" and places:[] those two fields are BOTH ZERO on a save that fills the entire province, while missing_cells=42846, stood_cells=42846 and derived_places=42 — and NONE of the seven audit fields is published by mapState() or getUIState().map. save/state.js:676 keeps only .dropped. This is round 1's remedy 1 and an S38 hard fail at the same time.

S38 VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not inherited: node tools/map/arbiter-map-s38.mjs is 6/6, exhaustive over all 42,846 of 42,846 generators, 0 unjustified squares, 0 out-of-sightline cells; --control=pre-s38 exits 1, red 4 of 6 against the historical loader. Clauses (a) and (b) genuinely hold.

Q1/Q2/Q3 SURVIVE S38 AND ARE NOT THE FORGED-SAVE QUESTION. S38-5 audits the MODEL's members (11 accessors, 0 write state). Neither it nor any other S38 assertion looks at the SLOT the model sits in. sim.discovery is writable+configurable, questEngine.sim === sim (3 squares) and window.__ENGINE reaches it outside every capability prohibition (2 squares) — a map with squares on it and NO claim to have stood anywhere, which is S38 clause (b) failing through a route the gate does not inspect.

undeclared_files_taken_and_why.why: RULE 28: declared here before writing, because I needed it and had not claimed it. `node tools/publish.mjs` is a gate and it FAILS CLOSED on a verdict whose piece id maps to no domain. W1-MAP-r2 is the first verdict in this series to carry a schema-1 `piece_id`, so `w1-map` was unmapped and publish exited 1. Added one line: 'w1-map': 'Controls & interface' — the same domain as w1-21, which owns the rest of the interface. I ALSO added 'w1-readables': 'Quests', which is NOT MINE: W1-READABLES-r2 was committed at 402d01a and was already failing the same gate before this round started, so publish was red for the whole fleet. A domain mapping cannot conflict semantically with its owner's work. Both entries carry a comment saying who added them and why. A THIRD entry, 'w1-road': 'The world', was added for W1-ROAD-JOIN, which landed from another agent while I was finishing and red-lined the same gate. Three unmapped pieces in one session: I have left a note in the file suggesting the table needs a default or a dispatch-time check, because the burden currently lands on whichever critic happens to publish next.
